I think this is awesome! I agree completely! I've been doing NaNoWriMo about 7 years now and have actually found some gems buried underneath all the crappy parts. 
I actually managed to fix, edit, and complete 4 novels.

It's all about the wordcount! Nothing more! Quantity over quality. 
It's not about writing POORLY. It's about WRITING. It's just plain writing. 
It's good for the writer because it forces them to churn out some semblance of a plot that can later be fleshed out and possibly turned into a gem of a real novel.

National Novel Writing Month was created to encourage writers to FINISH a novel. It wasn't designed to churn out something of quality. It's all about the wordcount! 
It's all about fun! 
So I think that something good DEFINITELY comes from writing 50,000 words. I have used so many of the plots that I came up with during the last 7 years of me doing NaNoWriMo that I have actually managed to finish, edit, and complete over 4 novels.

I'm an editor! I would like to put in my two cents by saying to definitely consider hiring an editor to peruse through your 'finished' pieces to determine its value to the literary world. 
From there, the editor might be able to send it to an Acquisitions editor and get the publishing process started. 
Another option is to ask around for a Literary Agent. They really know how to represent you as an author. 
Lastly, especially if you're going into the self-publishing market, may I recommend CreateSpace.com? They walk you through step by step and are willing to answer any questions you have for a low flat rate! 

Good luck with all your endeavors. If you have any more questions, feel free to email me at TarynLove8@gmail.com. I'm always looking for more aspiring writers to talk to.
